knowledge:
- key_parameters:
    - data (in PreFL()): Raw count data matrix (not relative abundance) to be filtered.
    - X (in PLSDA_batch()): CLR-transformed data matrix where rows are samples and columns are variables.
    - Y.trt (in PLSDA_batch()): Categorical factor representing the treatment effect of interest.
    - Y.bat (in PLSDA_batch()): Categorical factor representing the batch effect to be removed.
    - ncomp.trt (in PLSDA_batch()): Number of treatment-related components to retain. Recommended value is nlevels(Y.trt) - 1.
    - ncomp.bat (in PLSDA_batch()): Number of batch-related components to remove. Recommended value is nlevels(Y.bat) - 1.
    - mode (in PLSDA_batch()): Character string specifying "regression" (recommended default for >1.6.0) or "canonical" (to reproduce older versions <=1.6.0).
    - keepX.trt (in PLSDA_batch()): Numeric vector specifying the number of variables to select on each treatment component for sparse PLSDA-batch (sPLSDA-batch).
    - balance (in PLSDA_batch()): Logical value. Set to FALSE to enable weighted PLSDA-batch for unbalanced batch-by-treatment designs.
- alternatives:
    - mixOmics::pca(): Used for principal component analysis to visualize sample patterns.
    - mixOmics::tune.splsda(): Used to optimize the number of variables to select (keepX.trt) for sPLSDA-batch.
    - vegan::varpart(): Used for partial Redundancy Analysis (pRDA) to partition variance between treatment and batch.
    - pheatmap::pheatmap(): Used for hierarchical clustering visualization of samples.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing microbiome/metagenomics raw count data that suffer from batch effects, compositionality, and uneven library sizes, and when you need to correct the data prior to downstream classification or variable selection.
- pitfalls:
    - Do not apply PreFL() to relative abundance data; it is strictly designed for raw count data.
    - Ensure the correct offset is added before CLR transformation: use 1 for raw counts, and half of the minimum value for relative abundance data.
    - Avoid using "canonical" mode for batch correction unless reproducing legacy results, as "regression" mode is biologically more appropriate.
    - Do not use unweighted PLSDA-batch on highly unbalanced designs; set balance = FALSE to activate the weighted version.

workflows.name: microbiome_batch_correction
workflows.intent: Filter, transform, detect, correct, and assess batch effects in microbiome raw count data using PLSDA-batch or sPLSDA-batch.
input: ad.count (raw OTU/microbial count matrix with samples in rows and OTUs in columns)
ad.metadata (sample metadata containing treatment and batch factor variables)
workflows.stages:
1. Pre-filter raw count data using PreFL to remove low-abundance/rare OTUs.
2. Transform filtered counts using CLR transformation with an offset of 1 via mixOmics::logratio.transfo.
3. Detect batch effects using PCA (mixOmics::pca), boxplots (box_plot), density plots (density_plot), linear regression (linear_regres), and pRDA (vegan::varpart).
4. Correct batch effects using PLSDA_batch in regression mode (or sPLSDA_batch by specifying keepX.trt).
5. Assess correction performance using post-correction PCA, global explained variance (partVar_plot), and alignment scores (alignment_score).
workflows.code:
# 1. Pre-filtering
ad.filter.res <- PreFL(data = ad.count)
ad.filter <- ad.filter.res$data.filter

# 2. Transformation
ad.clr <- logratio.transfo(X = ad.filter, logratio = "CLR", offset = 1)
class(ad.clr) <- "matrix"

# 3. Batch effect detection
ad.pca.before <- mixOmics::pca(ad.clr, ncomp = 3, scale = TRUE)
Scatter_Density(
    components = ad.pca.before$variates$X, comp = c(1, 2),
    expl.var = ad.pca.before$prop_expl_var$X,
    batch = ad.batch, trt = ad.trt,
    title = "AD data", trt.legend.title = "Phenol conc."
)

ad.OTU.name <- selectVar(ad.pca.before, comp = 1)$name[1]
ad.OTU_batch <- data.frame(value = ad.clr[, ad.OTU.name], batch = ad.batch)
box_plot(
    df = ad.OTU_batch, title = paste(ad.OTU.name, "(AD data)"),
    x.angle = 30
)
density_plot(df = ad.OTU_batch, title = paste(ad.OTU.name, "(AD data)"))

ad.OTU.lm <- linear_regres(
    data = ad.clr[, ad.OTU.name],
    trt = ad.trt, batch.fix = ad.batch,
    type = "linear model"
)

ad.factors.df <- data.frame(trt = ad.trt, batch = ad.batch)
ad.rda.before <- varpart(ad.clr, ~trt, ~batch,
    data = ad.factors.df, scale = TRUE
)

# 4. Batch effect correction (PLSDA-batch)
ad.PLSDA_batch.res.reg <- PLSDA_batch(
    X = ad.clr,
    Y.trt = ad.trt, Y.bat = ad.batch,
    ncomp.trt = 1, ncomp.bat = 4,
    mode = "regression"
)
ad.PLSDA_batch.reg <- ad.PLSDA_batch.res.reg$X.nobatch

# 4. Batch effect correction (sPLSDA-batch)
ad.sPLSDA_batch.res.reg <- PLSDA_batch(
    X = ad.clr,
    Y.trt = ad.trt, Y.bat = ad.batch,
    ncomp.trt = 1, keepX.trt = 100,
    ncomp.bat = 4, mode = "regression"
)
ad.sPLSDA_batch.reg <- ad.sPLSDA_batch.res.reg$X.nobatch

# 5. Assessing batch effect correction
ad.prop.df <- data.frame(
    Treatment = NA, Batch = NA,
    Intersection = NA,
    Residuals = NA
)
for (i in seq_len(length(ad.corrected.list))) {
    rda.res <- varpart(ad.corrected.list[[i]], ~trt, ~batch,
        data = ad.factors.df, scale = TRUE
    )
    ad.prop.df[i, ] <- rda.res$part$indfract$Adj.R.squared
}
rownames(ad.prop.df) <- names(ad.corrected.list)
ad.prop.df <- ad.prop.df[, c(1, 3, 2, 4)]
partVar_plot(prop.df = ad.prop.df)

res <- alignment_score(
    data = ad.corrected.list[[i]],
    batch = ad.batch,
    var = 0.95,
    k = 8,
    ncomp = 50
)
